issue_context.title: Order of algorithms search
issue_context.body:
In 3.0 we can have an implementation provided by on of a native providers, by engine and by the 3rd-party provider at the same time. 

We should establish a unified order of selecting the implementation and use it consistently in all the places we directly  look for a presence of the algorithm.
comments:
Within the providers, there order is deliberately undefined.  Property queries should be used to pick a specific provider.

The question of engine vs provider is interesting.

The concept of priority of algorithms is something for post 3.0.

Current code works this way:
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/62829f9f26bf248f29be9604870bbe46f946927a/crypto/cms/cms_lib.c#L411-L424

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/62829f9f26bf248f29be9604870bbe46f946927a/apps/speed.c#L1498-L1512

@levitte says the order should be reverted (see https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/14182#issuecomment-779046452).

I anyway think we should get an unified code (helper functions) to ensure the order and avoid code duplication.

> Within the providers, there order is deliberately undefined. Property queries should be used to pick a specific provider.

Can we explicitly request "Use RSA from the provider XXX"? If yes, it solves the problem.

> Can we explicitly request "Use RSA from the provider XXX"? If yes, it solves the problem.

You can fetch a provider side algorithm based on properties.  Exactly what properties are available to query depends on the provider.  We *could* have apps choose to only fetch (i.e. not use functions like `EVP_get_digestbyname()` at all) if there is a property query string, even an empty one.

Looking more closely at this issue, I'm having misgivings about what the proper order is.

When looking at `apps/dgst.c`, I was previously thinking that since an engine must be explicitly loaded (via `-engine`), that signals an explicit desire to use that engine's implementations, so it would be natural to use `EVP_get_digestbyname()` first and `EVP_MD_fetch()` as a fallback.

However, if both providers and engines are loaded due to configuration in the config file, there's no indication from the user what's preferred, making the order harder to determine from user input.

So, if I can have a show of hands; if there's no way to say what the user prefers, do we:

-   Try fetching first, then fall back on legacy methods?, or
-   Try legacy methods first, then fall back on fetching?

It might be a good idea to have a look at the code for functions like `EVP_DigestInit_ex()` to see what priorities have been made there and if that can give an indication of what we should do.

My preference would be to fetch first and only if not found, fallback on legacy. And yes, I understand this will break some legacy use-cases as basically you won't be able to override provider implementation with engine implementation. But IMO this should be acceptable. Another possibility would be to look if we have any engine set up (by option or configuration) and in that case prefer the legacy, but that makes the behavior much less dependable.

I'd favour fetch then fallback too.

However, should we honour an engine based default (e.g. via `ENGINE_set_default_digests`)?  I think we ought to.  Which would be default -> fetch -> fallback.

> default -> fetch -> fallback.

Considering that "default" from ENGINEs is baked into "fallback", oh boy there's some dissection to do.  We might want to consider a libcrypto function that does this for us, uniformly...  that or allow EVP_XXX_fetch() to return legacy algorithms, but only if libctx and propq are NULL...  [duck, run]

> > default -> fetch -> fallback.
> 
> Considering that "default" from ENGINEs is baked into "fallback", oh boy there's some dissection to do. We might want to consider a libcrypto function that does this for us, uniformly... that or allow EVP_XXX_fetch() to return legacy algorithms, but only if libctx and propq are NULL... [duck, run]

Well... with the change to allow EVP_xxx_free() on the non-fetched algorithms it would actually be possible. :rofl:
Oh, and we get an universal API fetch - hash/cipher/etc - free? It's the API of my dream!

Whatever we do, the order should be deterministic and defined.

I'm much less concerned about where Engine fits into things as Engine is legacy and is going away or if we have different orders of processing compared to previous handling for engines in order to get something considered "logical" with providers. 

We should be able to specify which algorithms come from which providers using configuration - that is where we need to end up - and that is a journey. We should not be thinking "applications can do this themselves" as although they can, the concept of providers is to allow the end user of an application to be able to control which providers are used for which algorithms - and that means controlling things in configuration and not by having applications all having to add mechanisms to achieve that explicitly.

In terms of order of processing, fetch from providers then fall back to legacy and engines hanging off legacy seems to me to be the right approach for now. I do not thing we should be adjusting where engine kicks in at all. 

Having EVP fetch being able to return any algorithm implementation whether it is provider based, or legacy (and hence engine) does not seem unreasonable. And I don't think we would need to have that limited to libctx==NULL or propq==NULL either.

It would also ease things significantly for contexts where you want to add an implementation for a subset of things and not have to implement everything (as per other discussions where it is "everything" or "nothing" per publickey type). 

We should just be able to view things as "implementations" and not have applications having to make a distinction between what sort of implementation of something it is (provider, legacy, engine).

> It would also ease things significantly for contexts where you want to add an implementation for a subset of things and not have to implement everything (as per other discussions where it is "everything" or "nothing" per publickey type).

It's off topic here but EC  has some issues in this regards :(
Question answered, we all seem to agree to fetch first, and have `EVP_get_{cipher,digest}xxx` as a fallback.  Therefore closed
Reopening to fix after #14898 is merged.

review_comments: Is the purpose of "try ignore errors" to allow some string to be checked as first an MD and then a CIPHER?  Er, yuk. :)  I think it is more clear to add code that says "is this a {cipher,md}" without side-effects.
There are also other places in speed where the silent() is used. I am not going to change this.
Because the -evp argument can be either cipher or md. If it is an md we need to clear the errors from the failed attempt of fetching a cipher.
Should we have an internal function for this block of code.. It seems to be reproduced a bit (cms is doing this for example, p12 probaby also does this).
That should be a separate PR.
Hmmm, I wonder why it's acceptable to have a NULL digest algorithm...  that doesn't make much sense...
I don't think it is acceptable, and it should say "<NULL>" if so.
Repeat using valid markup: I don't think it is acceptable, and it should say `<NULL>` if so.  Not an empty string
The opt_md can be called in other places than just with an option argument. It might be that somebody passes NULL. I am also not changing this. If you want to, submit a new PR as this is unrelated.
Looking at `digest` and `md_alg`, it looks to me like one of them is redundant and can be removed completely.
